verdict.rationale: Cal.com's core and its cal.diy fork are publicly hosted on GitHub under open licenses (MIT for cal.diy, historically AGPL for the main repo), so the source code itself is readable and verifiable by anyone, corroborated by the GitHub repo description and independent self-host runtime probe successfully booting the published image. However, evidence also shows cal.diy explicitly strips 'enterprise/commercial code' from the main Cal.com repo (implying some features are closed-source) and community reports describe the AGPL as 'restrictive' and cite a 'bait-and-switch' reducing self-host support, which tempers but does not negate the underlying open-source readability of the codebase. Missing for 10: confirmation the entire feature set (including enterprise pieces) is open rather than split, and resolution of community concerns about license restrictiveness/trust.
